title: Using third-party packages and publishing a module of your own

videos.script: Lesson 39 split your own code into packages. This last lesson reaches outside your module. {{get}} First you take somebody else's package. go get chooses the version you depend on. The same command upgrades it, downgrades it and removes it. You will watch an upgrade change what a program prints, without one line of your code changing. {{choose}} Then the harder question: whether to depend on it at all. Who may use it, who still maintains it, and how much it drags in with it. And govulncheck, which tells you when a version you rely on has a known flaw, and which version fixes it. {{publish}} Last, the other side of the trade. You publish a module of your own. In Go there is nothing to upload. A version is a tag in a repository, and the proxy copies it. {{major}} And when you have to break a promise, the version number says so, and so does the import path. {{end}} That is the end of this course. You can write a Go program, organise it, depend on other people's code and share your own. Goroutines and channels are next, in the go-concurrency course.
